newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dlr ends at 7-mth low on Deng health report.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dlr ends at 7-mth low on Deng health report.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed at a seven-month low on Tuesday on reports that the deteriorating health of China paramount leader Deng Xiaoping had forced China leaders to cut short trips and return to Beijing, dealers said.
The local unit finished at T$27.648 against Monday's T$27.585 close.
Turnover through dealers was a hectic US$505 million.
Sources in Beijing on Monday said Deng's poor health had forced Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin and other leaders to cut short provincial trips to return to Beijing.

Dealers attributed the Taiwan dollar's sharp falls to concerns over Deng's deteriorating health and the central bank's repeated comments that the Taiwan dollar should follow the U.S. dollar's trend overseas.
Dealers have said the bank's call signalled further falls for the local currency.
"The U.S. dollar buying was very, very strong today," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
But the central bank had offered to sell the U.S. dollar in a bid to smooth the Taiwan dollar's depreciation, she added.
Dealers said the impact from Deng's reported poor health was expected to ease on Wednesday.
Initial support for the local currency was seen at T$27.70, with resistance expected at T$27.60.
